title: Text messages
description: Make a two-person exchange feel like texting, with alternating bubbles, timestamps, and delivery status.
tip: Duplicate an incoming or outgoing block for each message. Keep the sender labels even when the colors differ.

title: Group chat
description: Give an ensemble scene a channel, speaker accents, quoted replies, and reactions.
tip: Add one entry per message. Speaker names and quoted text carry the conversation when the skin is hidden.

title: Email correspondence
description: Tell a story through inbox headers, signatures, quoted replies, and an attachment label.
tip: Edit the From, To, Date, and Subject fields. The attachment is a text label; link a real file separately if needed.

title: Personal letter
description: Set a letter apart from the surrounding narration with warm paper, a dateline, and a handwritten-style signature.
tip: Replace the salutation, body, and signature. The handwriting uses fonts on the reader's device and falls back to cursive.

title: Journal entries
description: Mark time passing with dated entries, crossed-out words, and a marginal note.
tip: Duplicate an entry for each date. Use crossed-out text only where the original words are meant to remain readable.

title: Newspaper clipping
description: Deliver worldbuilding as an article, with a masthead, headline, byline, and columns that adapt to the available width.
tip: Change the publication and headline. Column width lets the article fall back to one column on narrow screens.

title: Case file
description: Frame evidence as a formal dossier, with numbered sections, metadata, and an explicit redaction.
tip: Replace the report fields and statements. [REDACTED] is literal text: no secret content is concealed by the CSS.

title: Social feed
description: Show public reactions through a platform-neutral feed of posts, nested replies, and quoted posts.
tip: Duplicate a post or reply block and edit the handles. Counts are part of the story text, not working social controls.

title: Recording transcript
description: Turn an interview, voicemail, or found recording into a readable transcript with timecodes and stage directions.
tip: Keep each timecode and speaker together. Put sounds, pauses, and missing audio in literal bracketed descriptions.

title: Terminal log
description: Give computer logs and recovered files a terminal treatment, with readable prompts, timestamps, and warning levels.
tip: Edit the static text; commands do not execute. Keep INFO and WARN labels so color never carries the whole meaning.

title: Poetry and lyrics
description: Control stanza rhythm and indentation while keeping line breaks in the text itself.
tip: Use a new paragraph for a stanza and a line break for a line. This sample uses Lorem ipsum, not quoted lyrics.

title: Chapter opening & scene breaks
description: Give a chapter a quiet opening: a title, epigraph, drop cap, and a clear divider between scenes.
tip: The initial is real text, not generated CSS content. The scene break uses a semantic horizontal rule.

title: Linked footnotes
description: Let readers follow an annotation and return to the exact reference, without scripts or pop-up windows.
tip: Keep each reference and note anchor paired. Give anchors unique names when repeating the template in one chapter.

title: Collapsible extras
description: Keep optional translations or extra notes close to the prose, in native panels readers can open themselves.
tip: Keep essential story content outside the panels. Open and close them with a click, Enter, or Space; no script is needed.
